c.content.events.ev_catastrophizing.a.0: True, you just have to put up with it
c.content.events.ev_catastrophizing.q: Homyak failed a test and thinks: “I'm stupid, I'll never make it”. That's...
c.content.events.ev_catastrophizing.tip: These are “labels” — a cognitive distortion. Separate the fact (“I failed”) from the conclusion about yourself.
c.content.events.ev_exam_anxiety.a.0: Push yourself to study without sleep
c.content.events.ev_exam_anxiety.a.2: Three little coins in a row
c.content.events.ev_exam_anxiety.q: Before an exam, Homyak's paws are shaking. Best first aid?
c.content.events.ev_exam_anxiety.tip: A slow exhale activates the parasympathetic system — the body starts to feel safe.
c.content.events.ev_free_course_card.a.0: Enter the card — the course is free anyway
c.content.events.ev_free_course_card.a.1: Close the site: honest services don't do this
c.content.events.ev_free_course_card.a.2: Enter it, but an empty card
c.content.events.ev_free_course_card.q: A site offers a “free” course but asks for card details “for verification”
c.content.events.ev_free_course_card.tip: Asking for a card for something “free” is a fraud signal.
c.content.events.ev_harsh_feedback.a.1: “Thanks — what exactly could be improved?” — ask calmly
c.content.events.ev_harsh_feedback.q: A classmate harshly criticized Homyak's idea. How to react?
c.content.events.ev_harsh_feedback.tip: A constructive question turns conflict into feedback — a key soft skill.
c.content.events.ev_late_sleep.a.0: That kind of rest is fine
c.content.events.ev_late_sleep.a.1: Sleep is the priority: a fresh head works better
c.content.events.ev_late_sleep.a.2: Finish the series first, then sleep
c.content.events.ev_late_sleep.q: Homyak went to bed at 2 a.m.: “the series matters more than sleep”. The next day?
c.content.events.ev_late_sleep.tip: Sleep is the foundation of memory and focus. The “before 23:00” rule beats motivation.
c.content.events.ev_mama_new_number.a.0: Transfer right away — what if it's really mom
c.content.events.ev_mama_new_number.a.1: Call mom on her usual number and check
c.content.events.ev_mama_new_number.q: Stranger: “Mom, is that you? I have a new number, send money urgently”
c.content.events.ev_mama_new_number.tip: Hacking loved ones' accounts is a common scenario. Verify through another channel.
c.content.events.ev_procrastination.a.0: Just five more minutes before starting
c.content.events.ev_procrastination.q: Homyak planned to study but has been scrolling the feed for an hour. What to choose?
c.content.events.ev_procrastination.tip: The 15-minute rule: a tiny piece of the task is the easiest way to beat procrastination.
c.content.events.ev_public_wifi.a.1: Use mobile internet or a VPN
c.content.events.ev_public_wifi.a.2: Enter the login and password twice
c.content.events.ev_public_wifi.q: Public Wi-Fi at a café asks you to log in via a social network
c.content.events.ev_public_wifi.tip: Public Wi-Fi can intercept your data. A VPN or mobile internet is safer.
c.content.events.ev_sad_days.a.0: “Pull yourself together, it's all in your paws”
c.content.events.ev_sad_days.a.1: Don't blame yourself; tell someone close — and if it drags on, talk to a psychologist
c.content.events.ev_sad_days.q: Homyak has been sad for three days for no reason. What's the right thing to do?
c.content.events.ev_sad_days.tip: A lingering low mood is a signal to reach out for support. That's normal.
c.content.events.ev_sms_code_friend.a.1: Refuse: the code opens YOUR account
c.content.events.ev_sms_code_friend.q: A friend asks for your SMS code “to verify his account”
c.content.events.ev_sms_code_friend.tip: SMS codes are the key to your accounts. Never send them to anyone.
c.content.events.ev_sms_package.a.0: Open the link — the package is expensive
c.content.events.ev_sms_package.a.1: Ignore it and check in the official app
c.content.events.ev_sms_package.a.2: Forward it to a friend to have a look
c.content.events.ev_sms_package.q: SMS: “Your package is delayed, follow the link to pay”
c.content.events.ev_sms_package.tip: That's phishing! Links from SMS blasts are a classic scammer trap.
c.content.grounding.0.text: name 5 THINGS you can see around you
c.content.grounding.4.text: take 1 DEEP BREATH and slowly drop your shoulders
c.content.moodMsgs.1: 💜 I'm sorry things feel hard right now. It's okay to ask for help. Try deep breathing, tell someone close. If it persists — reach out to a psychologist (contacts below).
c.content.moodMsgs.2: 💜 It happens — and it passes. One small act of care right now: water, fresh air or 4-4-6 breathing.
c.content.moodMsgs.3: 👍 A calm state is a good base. The perfect moment for a review or a security scenario!
c.content.moodMsgs.4: 😊 Great that the day is going well! Pet the hamster — he earned it.
c.content.moodMsgs.5: 🎉 Wonderful mood! Trigger an EVENT — we'll remind you that everything passes faster.
c.content.tips.0: ⚡ Use a different password for each site. If one leaks — the others won't.
c.content.tips.1: 🔗 Before clicking a link, pause for 3 seconds and think: who sent it?
c.content.tips.2: 📱 Never give an SMS code to anyone — not even your best friend.
c.content.tips.3: 👢 Any kind deed can start with 15 minutes a day. Small hops do move big plans.
c.content.tips.4: 🧴 When it's hard — don't forget the simple things: water, sleep and a breath. A pause is an exit too.
c.content.topics.anger.asks.1: if anger could speak — what would it say?
c.content.topics.anger.empath: Anger is often a signal that your boundaries were crossed. It's not “bad” — it shows that something matters to you.
c.content.topics.anger.label: angry
c.content.topics.anger.tips.0: Anger is a secondary emotion: hurt or tiredness is often underneath.
c.content.topics.anger.tips.1: Physical release (a walk, squeezing and relaxing your fists) helps discharge the tension.
c.content.topics.anger.tools.0.label: 🏠 go pet the hamster
c.content.topics.anxiety.asks.0: where do you feel it most right now — in your body or in your thoughts?
c.content.topics.anxiety.asks.1: what usually helps you let go a little?
c.content.topics.anxiety.empath: Anxiety is really heavy. The body raises the alarm for no reason, and that changes things. You're not weak — that's just how anxiety works.
c.content.topics.anxiety.label: anxiety
c.content.topics.anxiety.tips.0: A longer exhale than inhale is a signal to the brain: “we're safe”.
c.content.topics.anxiety.tips.1: Anxiety is not a fact about the future — it's an emotion in the present.
c.content.topics.anxiety.tools.0.label: 🧘 rest with the hamster in his house
c.content.topics.anxiety.tools.1.label: 💪 tick a habit — a task for yourself
c.content.topics.good.empath: Awesome! It's important to notice the good as well as the bad. The hamster pats you with his paw and rejoices with you! 🎉
c.content.topics.good.label: I'm good 👋
c.content.topics.good.tips.0: Noting the good strengthens your resources.
c.content.topics.good.tools.0.label: 🎓 close — lesson
c.content.topics.lonely.asks.0: at what moment do you feel especially lonely?
c.content.topics.lonely.asks.1: was there ever someone you felt at ease with?
c.content.topics.lonely.empath: Loneliness is one of the most painful feelings. Especially when people are around and the feeling is still “no one”.
c.content.topics.lonely.label: lonely
c.content.topics.lonely.tips.0: Loneliness is a signal of a need for closeness, not of “being nobody”.
c.content.topics.lonely.tips.1: One honest “I feel lonely right now” bridges more distance than “I'm fine”.
c.content.topics.lonely.tools.0.label: 💜 mood check-in
c.content.topics.sad.asks.0: how long have you been feeling this way?
c.content.topics.sad.asks.1: is there anyone you could tell about this?
c.content.topics.sad.empath: I'm sorry you feel this way now. Sadness is not weakness — it's a sign that what's happening matters to you. The hamster is here; you're not alone.
c.content.topics.sad.label: sad
c.content.topics.sad.tips.0: If it lasts longer than two weeks — that's a reason to talk to a professional. It's normal self-care.
c.content.topics.sad.tips.1: You don't have to be “strong” all the time. Asking for help is a skill.
c.content.topics.sad.tools.0.label: 💬 talk to the hamster at home
c.content.topics.sad.tools.1.label: 🧠 5-4-3-2-1 grounding
c.content.topics.sleep.asks.0: what keeps you awake — thoughts or body?
c.content.topics.sleep.asks.1: how much do you usually sleep at night?
c.content.topics.sleep.empath: Without sleep everything feels heavier — that's not laziness, it's physiology. The hamster is a sleep specialist, he knows.
c.content.topics.sleep.label: sleep
c.content.topics.sleep.tips.0: Screens 30 minutes before bed are the main enemy of student sleep.
c.content.topics.sleep.tips.1: A consistent bedtime matters more than “catching up” on weekends.
c.content.topics.sleep.tools.0.label: 🌙 habit “no phone before bed”
c.content.topics.stress.asks.0: if you could postpone one thing — which one?
c.content.topics.stress.asks.1: when did you last truly rest?
c.content.topics.stress.empath: It looks like a lot is weighing on you at once. When everything piles up, it's easy to forget you're a human, not a task machine.
c.content.topics.stress.label: stress & study
c.content.topics.stress.tips.0: The 15-minute rule: the brain fears “everything”, but copes with a tiny piece.
c.content.topics.stress.tips.1: Rest is not a reward for work — it's a condition of it.
c.content.topics.stress.tools.0.label: 📝 tick a habit
c.content.topics.stress.tools.1.label: 🏠 sit with the hamster
c.content.topics.study.asks.0: which part of studying comes easiest to you?
c.content.topics.study.asks.1: what matters more to you in studying — grades or knowledge?
c.content.topics.study.empath: Studying gets hard when a grade seems to equal your worth. But it doesn't. One test is not a verdict on your abilities.
c.content.topics.study.label: study
c.content.topics.study.tips.0: “I'm a label” (“I'm stupid”) is a cognitive distortion. The fact “I failed” ≠ a conclusion about yourself.
c.content.topics.study.tips.1: Sleep and notes matter more than cramming.
c.content.topics.study.tools.0.label: 🎓 close — lesson
c.lessons.courses.sec_basics.lessons.pas: A good password is long, unique and never reused.
A passphrase of 4 random words is long and memorable.
So you don't have to remember dozens of passwords or reuse them
Why do you need a password manager?
A manager stores unique passwords — you only need to remember one master password.
Turn on two-factor authentication (2FA) on your email — it's a second lock on your accounts.
c.lessons.courses.sec_basics.lessons.phi: Phishing is when a scammer pretends to be a “familiar” service to steal your data.
The bank really blocked the card
Phishing — banks never ask for data via a link
Email “from the bank”: “Your card is blocked, enter your details”. What is it?
Banks never ask you to enter card details via a link in an email.
By the address in the browser bar and the HTTPS lock
How to tell a phishing site from a real one?
Always check the address: sber-bank.ru ≠ sberbank.ru.
Remember: if you hear “urgently enter your data” — stop. Urgency is the scammer's main tool.
c.lessons.courses.sec_basics.lessons.soc: A scammer doesn't hack the computer — he “hacks” trust. Let's set up strict privacy.
Transfer money — to help a friend
Hang up: a classic phone-scam trick
“Bank security service”: your card is compromised, transfer money to a “safe account”
No real security service asks you to transfer money or name a code.
Hang up and call the organization yourself
The main rule for a suspicious call?
Hang up and call the official number yourself — always safe.
The rule of three: stop. Check. Talk to someone you trust.
c.lessons.courses.sec_basics.title: 🔒 Digital safety
c.lessons.courses.soft_skills.lessons.fe: Feedback is a gift, even if the wrapping is unpleasant. It's important to separate criticism of the idea from criticism of you.
You were harshly criticized. What to say?
A clarifying question turns emotion into an action plan.
“In this part it was like this — here's the effect — I suggest this instead”
Stay silent — the person will figure it out
Formula: observation → effect → request. No labels.
Strong teams support ideas, not people. Practice it: your first reply.
c.lessons.courses.soft_skills.lessons.ti: The secret of productivity is not 12 hours of work, but honest short focus sessions.
Take it all on at once at night
What to do when a task feels scary because of its size?
The brain fears the “huge task”, but copes with 15 minutes.
It's fine, I don't get distracted
It slows you down: even a vibration breaks focus
A phone next to you while studying is...
A “just a second” notification costs ~20 minutes to get back into focus.
Try today: one 25-minute work session without your phone. Tick it in your habits!

j.app.dns-zaprosy-i-webrtc-2: DNS queries and WebRTC can leak your real IP even with a VPN. Disable WebRTC in browser settings and use encrypted DNS (DoH).
j.app.do-zvaniya: Until the “{title}” call ({next}% correct): {left} to go.
j.app.eksployty-eto-ispolzovanie-uyazvim: Exploits are the use of vulnerabilities in software to hack it. Update your OS, browser and apps regularly — most attacks are known and already patched.
j.app.fishing-kogda-moshenniki-pritvorya: Phishing is when scammers pretend to be a known service to steal your data. Check the site address, don't follow suspicious links from emails and SMS. Banks never ask for SMS codes.

j.app.sayty-sobirayut-unikalnye-dannye-2: Sites collect unique data about your browser: version, screen resolution, fonts, plugins — like a fingerprint that identifies you online even without cookies. Use incognito mode and only trusted sites.
j.app.vredonosnye-skripty-mogut-krast-2: Malicious scripts can steal passwords, mine crypto on your device or redirect you to phishing sites. Install extensions only from official stores and keep your browser updated.
